subject: Scope and mechanics for tenant-held keys and operator access — DPA confirmation
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha@medsync.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: rajesh@medsync.com
Date: Mon, 12 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment DPA questions — BYOK, subprocessors, cross-border

Sean,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — MedSync is excited about the Private deployment option. Before we proceed to procurement, our legal/security team has a few questions we need to clarify in the DPA/SOW:

1) Customer-controlled keys (BYOK): we need confirmation you support a tenant-held HSM-backed KMS where keys never leave our control. Please outline any operator/system access patterns (eg. break-glass, emergency unseal) and the approval workflow for that access.

2) Subprocessors: provide the current subprocessor roster for the Private offering and your proposed notice and objection periods. We will need subprocessor commitments scoped by region (EU/US/APAC) for data residency compliance.

3) Cross-border transfers: for EU-data in the service, confirm the legal mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, etc.) and whether any telemetry/metrics leave the VPC for product analytics.

4) Auditability & logs: what logs are retained, who can access them, and can we require a separate audit stream for our tenant?

5) Escrow / operator access: MedSync legal has historically required an emergency access escrow for very small set of circumstances; please state Redwood's stance and the conditionality for granting operator access.

Attached is a short summary of what the procurement team will need. Can we schedule a call this week with your legal/infra folks to run through items 1–5 and get a DPA draft in flight?

Thanks,
Asha Reddy
Counsel, MedSync Solutions
asha@medsync.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: MedSync_Reqs_Summary_20270912.pdf (doc stub)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@medsync.com>
Cc: rajesh@medsync.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA questions — BYOK, subprocessors, cross-border

Asha — thanks for the clear list and for the fast follow. High level answers inline; happy to follow up on a call this week with our legal and infra leads.

1) BYOK: Redwood supports tenant-held keys via customer-managed KMS (HSM-backed). Keys can be configured so they are only referenced by the private deployment gateway in your VPC; Redwood’s control plane never stores plaintext keys. We do have an operator break-glass capability for emergency incident response; that path is tightly controlled (two-person approval, limited duration, fully audited).

2) Subprocessors: I’ve attached our current subprocessor CSV and a draft DPA for your review. Standard practice is 30 days' notice of new subprocessors and a right to object; we can discuss extended notice for specific vendors.

3) Cross-border: For EU-origin data we rely on SCCs where applicable and can support in-region routing. Product telemetry is pseudonymized and aggregated; we do not include raw tenant data in analytics. We can arrange a per-tenant telemetry export/stream if you want a separate audit-only view.

4) Logs: operator actions and system logs are retained and can be routed to your logging endpoints. We log break-glass events with full context and can provide audit reports on request.

5) Escrow: we have an emergency access playbook; escrow arrangements are exceptional and require legal review. We are open to discussing a scoped escrow or custodian arrangement under a narrowly defined protocol.

I’ve attached: Redwood_DPA_Draft_20270912.pdf and subprocessors_20270912.csv.

If it works, let’s book Wed 09/14 10:00 PT for a legal+infra call. If that’s tight, propose alternatives.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0104

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Draft_20270912.pdf (attachment stub), subprocessors_20270912.csv (attachment stub)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Sep 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment DPA questions — MedSync (need legal & privacy stance)

Team — forwarding MedSync's note and the draft DPA/subprocessor list. Key asks: tenant-held KMS with details on operator break-glass, escrow ask, and regional subprocessor visibility/notice. 

Questions:
- Can we accept an escrow arrangement under controlled conditions?
- Are our current break-glass controls (2-person approval, logged, time-limited) sufficient for legal, or do we need changes?
- Any specific redlines we should preemptively push in the DPA for cross-border wording?

MedSync is a strategic prospect in healthcare (PHI-adjacent workloads) so this one will likely need stricter guarantees. Please advise and, if possible, redline the attached DPA. I can join the call with Asha on Wed.

Thanks —Sean

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Sep 2027 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment DPA questions — MedSync (need legal & privacy stance)

Sean / Grace — see legal position below and attached redline. Summary:

- BYOK: Acceptable. We will require an HSM-backed key configuration and explicit DPA language that keys are customer-controlled; add a clause that Redwood will not export or persist key material outside customer boundary.
- Break-glass / operator access: We can accept a limited break-glass with two-person approval, strictly scoped to incident response (security remediation, data recovery) and time-boxed (max 4 hours per event unless further legal approval). All sessions must be recorded and logs retained. Add notification to customer within 24 hours of any break-glass event.
- Escrow: We do not prefer open escrow. If MedSync insists, we can consider a third-party escrow agent with narrowly defined conditions (court order or mutually-agreed emergency criteria). Any escrow process must include cryptographic proof-of-release and an audit trail.
- Subprocessors & notice: Standard 30-day notice with right to object on reasonable grounds. For regulated customers, we can offer an extended notice period or a carve-out requiring consent for specific categories (eg., off-shore telemetry vendors).
- Cross-border: We will commit to SCCs for transfers from EU to US where required and to in-region routing for EU-resident deployments. Telemetry: agree to pseudonymize and aggregate for product analytics; offer dedicated telemetry pipeline to customer for audit-only.

I attached a redline of the DPA with proposed language for the above. If MedSync wants escrow, legal will need to negotiate the escrow instrument and access triggers.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redline_20270913_legal.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Asha Reddy <asha@medsync.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: rajesh@medsync.com
Date: Thu, 15 Sep 2027 07:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA questions — follow up after legal review

Sean — appreciate the quick turnaround and Lauren’s redline. A few follow ups after internal review at MedSync legal/security:

• Escrow: MedSync prefers an escrow arrangement for emergency operator access with a neutral third-party custodian. The trigger would be a verified incident where our key-holder cannot respond (eg. key compromise or catastrophic loss) or a court order. We’d like clear technical controls for escrow release (multi-sig + proof-of-release).

• Break-glass window: MedSync asks for a clear retention window for break-glass session footage and audit logs; we typically request 7 years for healthcare compliance.

• Subprocessors: please confirm no subprocessors in APAC that process EU-data. Also request the ability to require subprocessor regional restrictions by adding a schedule to the DPA.

• Telemetry: confirm that raw request payloads are never included in product analytics; aggregated metrics only. If logs need to be used to troubleshoot at support’s request, we need explicit consent and an approval flow.

Happy to discuss on Fri 09/16; Rajesh and I are available 10:00–12:00 PT.

Best,
Asha
Counsel, MedSync Solutions

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@medsync.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Sep 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA questions — proposed alignment and next steps

Asha — thanks, and appreciated the specificity from MedSync. We can align on the following items; I’ve summarized the proposed contractual/operational language below and attached an updated DPA for signature if helpful.

1) Escrow: willing to accept a third-party escrow arrangement limited to emergency key recovery where the customer key-holder is demonstrably unavailable or under a lawful order. Escrow release requires multi-sig from escrow agent plus an authorization workflow involving Redwood and MedSync legal; all releases will generate cryptographic proof-of-release and a full audit bundle.

2) Break-glass retention: Redwood will retain break-glass session recordings and related audit logs for 7 years and provide certified reports on request. Notification to customer within 24 hours of any event remains in place.

3) Subprocessors & regional scoping: confirm there are currently no APAC subprocessors touching EU-origin data for this Private offering. We will include a Regional Subprocessors schedule in the DPA and commit to 30 days' notice for additions; for named critical vendors we can add a consent carve-out.

4) Telemetry & support access: raw tenant request payloads are excluded from product analytics. Support access to logs for troubleshooting is available only via a documented approval flow (customer consent or a support ticket with customer approver).

Next steps: I’m attaching Redwood_DPA_FinalProposed_20270916.pdf with these commitments included. If this aligns, we can execute via DocuSign (link below) and schedule an operational kickoff and key-handshake runbook session (recommended attendees: MedSync infra, Redwood infra, legal). Proposed DocuSign bundle: DPA + SOW + Subprocessor schedule.

—Sean
